name: gdb
one_line: Run a program under a debugger: stop it, look at registers and memory, step instruction by instruction.
plain: Run a program under a debugger: stop it, look at registers and memory, step instruction by instruction.
The sections below show when to use it, real examples, and the options explained in plain English.
when: Binary exploitation: find the offset that overwrites the return address.
Reverse engineering: watch what a check compares.
See what a crashed program was doing.

examples.title: Break at main and look at registers
examples.output: (expected, not captured) Breakpoint 1, 0x... in main () followed by a line like rip 0x55555555513d showing the instruction pointer.

examples.title: Disassemble main in Intel syntax
examples.output: (expected, not captured) Assembly of main with addresses, including a call to strcmp and a conditional jump.

examples.title: Crash it and read the registers
examples.output: (expected, not captured) Possibly no crash for this program; for a vulnerable one: Program received signal SIGSEGV and rip showing the overwritten value (such as 0x4141414141414141).

examples.title: Print a string from memory
examples.output: (expected, not captured) A line starting with the address and the bytes at it interpreted as text or instructions.

options.plain: Step over / into a call; by source line or instruction

options.use: Where is the program, what are the values
Look at the stack, strings or code

options.flag: pattern create N / pattern offset X

mistakes: Stack addresses in gdb differ from the real run (environment size and path): sweep or leak the real address.
gdb disables ASLR by default; the real program may randomise.
Set-uid programs lose privileges under gdb.
Install pwndbg or GEF for a readable display.
try: Find which instruction of `hello` compares your argument.
Change `argv[1]` in memory so the check passes.
Use `x/20wx $rsp` to dump the stack at `main`.
see_also: pwndbg / GEF, objdump, ltrace / strace, ghidra, pwntools.
captured_with: Examples marked expected were not captured yet (gdb not installed here); run scripts/atlas_build.py where the tool is installed (Kali) to capture real output.
